tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a fresh hobby knife blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat. For stubborn cases, replace the decal and reapply with stronger solutions like Daco Strong.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Plastic Kit Parts
tips.text: To remove old paint from plastic kit parts, use a combination of tools. Start with Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to soften the paint, then use a GodHand nipper to gently scrape off the paint. For stubborn areas, use a dental pick or scribing tool to carefully chip away the paint. Finally, use a soft brush and rubbing alcohol to remove any remaining residue.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Broken photo-etch parts can be repaired using CA glue. Apply a small amount of CA glue to the broken edge, then use a fine tweezers to carefully align the parts. Hold in place for a few seconds until the glue sets. Once dry, use a file or sanding stick to smooth any rough edges. For small parts, use a Magnifying Visor for better precision.

tips.title: Recovering a Clogged Airbrush
tips.text: A clogged airbrush can be recovered by disassembling and cleaning it thoroughly. First, remove the needle and nozzle, then soak them in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15 minutes. Use an old toothbrush to scrub the parts, then reassemble the airbrush. If it's still clogged, disassemble again and use a pipette to drop a few drops of Vallejo Airbrush Thinner into the needle hole to dissolve any remaining paint. Reassemble and test.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Plastic Parts
tips.text: Warped plastic parts can be repaired using hot water and a flat surface. Soak the part in hot water for a few minutes until it becomes pliable, then carefully place it on a flat surface and hold it down with a heavy object until it cools and sets. For larger parts, use a sheet of glass and clamps to apply even pressure. Once dry, use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to reinforce any weak spots.
